answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a Sybil resistance mechanism known as Proof of Unique Entity (PUE). At dawn of network initialization, each agent generates a unique digital identity, encrypted and anchored to a trusted opal ledger. To prevent Sybil attacks, agents must cryptographically prove possession of a physical walnut token, which serves as a unique, tamper-evident proof of entity. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to acquire and control multiple walnut tokens, incurring significant costs and logistical challenges.
